title: 家人、鄰居與家裡
subtitle: Family, neighbours and things around the house

example.gloss: The beef noodles Grandma makes are the tastiest.

example.hanzi: 叔叔開車送我去捷運站。
example.pinyin: Shúshu kāichē sòng wǒ qù jiéyùn zhàn.

vocab.gloss: to take care of; to show consideration; to attend to

example.hanzi: 媽媽生病的時候,爸爸在家照顧她。
example.pinyin: Māma shēngbìng de shíhòu, bàba zài jiā zhàogù tā.
example.gloss: When Mom was sick, Dad stayed home and took care of her.

vocab.gloss: to help; to lend a hand; to do a favor

example.pinyin: Míngtiān nǐ kěyǐ lái bāngmáng ma?
example.gloss: Can you come and help out tomorrow?

grammar.title: 幫忙 and 幫 + person + verb
grammar.pattern: 幫 + 人 + (一個忙 / 動詞短語) ; 幫忙 + 動詞
grammar.explanation: 幫忙 is a verb-object word (幫 + 忙), so it cannot take a person after it. If you want to say who you are helping, put that person right after 幫: 幫我、幫奶奶. You can then add what you do for them: 幫奶奶買菜. 幫忙 stands alone (你來幫忙) or comes before another verb (幫忙照顧爺爺).
grammar.contrast: 幫忙照顧 vs 幫我照顧: use 幫忙 + verb when nobody is named; the moment you name the person being helped, drop 忙 and say 幫 + 人 + verb.
grammar.common_error: Learners say 幫忙我買菜 because 'help me' feels like one word. 忙 is already the object of 幫, so a person can't follow it — say 幫我買菜 or 幫我一個忙.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kěyǐ bāng wǒ yí ge máng ma?
examples.gloss: Can you do me a favor?

examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒ bāng nǎinai mǎi cài.
examples.gloss: On the weekend I buy groceries for Grandma.

examples.hanzi: 叔叔常常來幫忙照顧爺爺。
examples.pinyin: Shúshu chángcháng lái bāngmáng zhàogù yéye.

passage.title: 回台中看爺爺奶奶
passage.hanzi: 我家住在台北,爺爺奶奶住在台中。每個月我都會搭火車回去看他們。爺爺最疼我,常常買我愛吃的水果。奶奶做的牛肉麵最好吃。上個月奶奶的腳很疼,叔叔就住在旁邊,每天幫忙照顧她。現在奶奶好多了,我週末回去的時候,也會幫她做點事。
passage.gloss: My family lives in Taipei, and my grandparents live in Taichung. Every month I take the train back to see them. Grandpa dotes on me the most and often buys the fruit I love. Grandma's beef noodles are the best. Last month Grandma's leg hurt a lot; my uncle lives right next door, so he helped take care of her every day. Now Grandma is much better, and when I go back on weekends I help her with a few things too.

grammar.title: 把 sentences: 把 + object + verb + result
grammar.pattern: Subject + 把 + object + verb + (到/開/完/出去…)
grammar.explanation: When you do something to a specific thing and change where it is or what state it's in, put the object right after 把, before the verb. The verb cannot stand alone — it needs a result: a destination (搬到樓上), a resultative word (打開、洗乾淨), or 了/完. The object must be something both speakers already know about (this table, the light), not just any table.
grammar.contrast: Plain Subject + Verb + Object (我搬桌子) simply names the activity. Use 把 when you want to say what happened to that specific object — 我把桌子搬到樓上 tells the listener where it ended up. If there is no result or change, don't use 把.
grammar.common_error: Learners stop after the verb and say 我把桌子搬 or 我把燈打, which sounds unfinished in Chinese. A 把 sentence must end with a result: 搬到樓上、搬出去、打開、洗乾淨、搬完了.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ zhuōzi bān dào lóushàng le.

examples.hanzi: 房間太黑了，請你把燈打開。
examples.pinyin: Fángjiān tài hēi le, qǐng nǐ bǎ dēng dǎkāi.

examples.hanzi: 鄰居幫我把舊的椅子搬出去了。

dialogue.speaker: 林太太
dialogue.hanzi: 你好，我們今天剛搬來，是你們的新鄰居。
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ hǎo, wǒmen jīntiān gāng bān lái, shì nǐmen de xīn línjū.

dialogue.hanzi: 歡迎歡迎！我住三樓。搬東西要幫忙嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Huānyíng huānyíng! Wǒ zhù sān lóu. Bān dōngxi yào bāngmáng ma?

dialogue.speaker: 林太太
dialogue.hanzi: 謝謝，桌子和椅子都搬完了，房子也洗乾淨了。
dialogue.pinyin: Xièxie, zhuōzi hé yǐzi dōu bān wán le, fángzi yě xǐ gānjìng le.
dialogue.gloss: Thanks, the tables and chairs are all moved in, and we've cleaned the place too.

dialogue.speaker: 王先生
dialogue.hanzi: 這條街道很安靜，晚上路燈也很亮，你們會住得很舒服。
dialogue.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiēdào hěn ānjìng, wǎnshàng lùdēng yě hěn liàng, nǐmen huì zhù de hěn shūfú.
dialogue.gloss: This street is very quiet, and the streetlights are bright at night — you'll live comfortably here.

dialogue.speaker: 林太太
dialogue.hanzi: 太好了！我們舊的地方車子太多。
dialogue.pinyin: Tài hǎo le! Wǒmen jiù de dìfāng chēzi tài duō.
dialogue.gloss: That's great! Our old place had way too much traffic.

dialogue.speaker: 王先生
dialogue.hanzi: 有事情就叫我啊，我就住在旁邊。
dialogue.pinyin: Yǒu shìqíng jiù jiào wǒ a, wǒ jiù zhù zài pángbiān.
dialogue.gloss: Just call me if you need anything — I live right next door.

sentences.gloss: We're moving into the new place this weekend.

passage.title: 新家與新鄰居
passage.hanzi: 上個週末我們搬家了。新家在一條安靜的街道上，附近有郵局、書店和一家麵店。房子不新，可是很乾淨，客廳的燈也很亮。舊家離公司太遠，現在我騎腳踏車十分鐘就到了。鄰居很熱情，昨天還送我們一袋水果，跟我們說有事情就叫他們。
passage.gloss: We moved last weekend. Our new home is on a quiet street, and nearby there's a post office, a bookstore, and a noodle shop. The house isn't new, but it's very clean, and the living-room light is bright. Our old place was too far from the office; now I ride my bike and get there in ten minutes. The neighbors are warm — yesterday they even brought us a bag of fruit and told us to call them if we ever need anything.

example.pinyin: Wǒ māma zài chúfáng zuò cài.
example.gloss: My mom is cooking in the kitchen.

example.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ yǒu hěn duō shuǐguǒ.
example.gloss: There's a lot of fruit in the fridge.

example.gloss: The fish at the market is very fresh.

example.pinyin: Wǒ de kāfēi bú yào jiā táng.
example.gloss: I don't want sugar in my coffee.

grammar.title: The 把 construction: moving or changing a known thing
grammar.pattern: Subject + 把 + (definite) Object + Verb + result / place / 了
grammar.explanation: 把 pulls the object in front of the verb so you can say what happened to it. Use it when the object is something both speakers already know about (那條魚, 我的碗) and the verb does something to it — moves it, cleans it, eats it up. The verb almost never stands alone: it needs a result, a place, or at least 了 after it. This is the everyday way to give kitchen instructions in Taiwan.
grammar.contrast: Plain S + V + O (我洗碗了) states the activity; 把 (我把碗洗乾淨了) focuses on one specific object and its new state. If the object is new or general ("some bowls", "a fish"), you cannot use 把 — say 我買了一條魚, not 我把一條魚買了.
grammar.common_error: Learners leave the verb bare — saying 我把碗洗 or 請把水果放 — which sounds unfinished. A 把 sentence needs something after the verb: 洗乾淨了, 放進冰箱, 吃完了.

examples.hanzi: 請把新鮮的魚放進冰箱。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ xīnxiān de yú fàng jìn bīngxiāng.
examples.gloss: Please put the fresh fish in the fridge.

examples.hanzi: 我把廚房的碗洗乾淨了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ chúfáng de wǎn xǐ gānjìng le.
examples.gloss: I washed the kitchen bowls clean.

examples.hanzi: 他把糖加到茶裡，茶太甜了。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ táng jiā dào chá lǐ, chá tài tián le.
examples.gloss: He added the sugar into the tea, and the tea got too sweet.

dialogue.speaker: 媽媽
dialogue.hanzi: 你去廚房幫我拿三個碗，好嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Nǐ qù chúfáng bāng wǒ ná sān ge wǎn, hǎo ma?

dialogue.hanzi: 好。媽，冰箱裡的魚還新鮮嗎？
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo. Mā, bīngxiāng lǐ de yú hái xīnxiān ma?
dialogue.gloss: Sure. Mom, is the fish in the fridge still fresh?

dialogue.speaker: 媽媽
dialogue.pinyin: Zǎoshang gāng mǎi de, hěn xīnxiān.
dialogue.gloss: I just bought it this morning, it's very fresh.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.hanzi: 那我們晚餐吃魚。我的茶要加一點糖。
dialogue.pinyin: Nà wǒmen wǎncān chī yú. Wǒ de chá yào jiā yìdiǎn táng.
dialogue.gloss: Then let's have fish for dinner. I want a little sugar in my tea.

dialogue.speaker: 媽媽
dialogue.pinyin: Jiā tài duō táng bù hǎo, huì tài tián.
dialogue.gloss: Too much sugar isn't good, it'll be too sweet.

dialogue.speaker: 小明
dialogue.pinyin: Hǎo ba, nà wǒ bù jiā le.
dialogue.gloss: Fine, then I won't add any.

sentences.gloss: Mom is washing bowls in the kitchen.

sentences.pinyin: Bīngxiāng lǐ de niúnǎi hěn xīnxiān.
sentences.gloss: The milk in the fridge is very fresh.

sentences.pinyin: Wǒ de chá bù jiā táng.
sentences.gloss: I don't put sugar in my tea.

sentences.pinyin: Zhè bēi chá tài tián le.
sentences.gloss: This cup of tea is too sweet.

sentences.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ wǎn fàng zài zhuōzi shàng.
sentences.gloss: Please put the bowls on the table.

passage.title: 我家的廚房
passage.hanzi: 我家的廚房不大，可是很乾淨。媽媽每天早上先去市場買菜，回家就把新鮮的魚和菜放進冰箱。晚上我們一起做飯，我幫媽媽洗碗。爸爸很愛喝茶，他的茶要加一點糖，他說這樣比較甜，也比較好喝。吃完飯，廚房又乾淨了。
passage.gloss: My family's kitchen isn't big, but it's very clean. Every morning Mom goes to the market to buy food first, and when she gets home she puts the fresh fish and vegetables into the fridge. In the evening we cook together, and I help Mom wash the bowls. Dad loves drinking tea; his tea needs a little sugar — he says it's sweeter that way, and tastes better. After we finish eating, the kitchen is clean again.
